sections.h2: Where does an Alpharetta seller start?
sections.html:
Owners here can hire a listing agent, sell privately, or accept a cash purchase on a closing date they pick. With a typical home value of $649,000 in Census figures, even small differences in condition and timing can move the final number a long way.

Alpharetta lies in the northern part of Fulton County, some 26 miles up from downtown Atlanta. It went by Milton until July 1858, was chartered as Alpharetta on December 11, 1858, and served as the seat of Milton County until 1931, when that county folded into Fulton to avoid bankruptcy during the Great Depression.

The city spans 26.9 square miles of land, with Johns Creek, Roswell and Milton as neighbors and unincorporated Forsyth County to the northeast. The climate is humid subtropical and falls in USDA hardiness zone 7b, which shapes what landscaping lasts and how mature trees shade a lot.

  • Listing pays off for a move-in ready house that can be staged for several bidders.
  • A private sale suits an owner who can price from nearby closed sales and has an attorney ready.
  • A cash sale helps with a probate property, a house needing big updates, or a relocation with little lead time.

sections.h2: What do Alpharetta's Census figures reveal about its housing?
sections.html:
This is an owner-occupied, high-income city. The July 2025 estimate is 66,921 residents, up 1.7 percent from the 65,810 base used for April 2020.

About 27.8 percent of residents were born abroad, and 32.8 percent of residents aged five and up use another language at home, which fits the global employers based in town.

sections.h2: Which companies and amenities bring buyers to Alpharetta?
sections.html:
Corporate offices lead the list. City economic development figures from February 2026 show Fiserv with 2,087 employees, ADP with 2,074, MCI (Verizon) with 1,928 and Equifax with 1,722, followed by Jackson Healthcare, Morgan Stanley, UPS Supply Chain Solutions, Toyota Motor Credit and Ernst and Young.

Downtown Alpharetta, the 86-acre Avalon district that opened in 2014, and the City Center complex add walkable dining and shopping, while North Point Mall is set for redevelopment. The Big Creek Greenway and the Alpha Loop, a trail system that now runs more than six miles, give neighborhoods near the paths a recreation draw.

No MARTA trains stop in Alpharetta, though bus routes link it to the rest of metro Atlanta. The Census Bureau puts the average commute for working residents at 26.3 minutes each way, a figure that belongs in a listing for houses near the major employers.

sections.h2: What local history and events add to Alpharetta's pull?
sections.html:
Alpharetta mixes new office parks with older landmarks. The Simeon and Jane Rucker Log House, built in 1833, was added to the federal register of historic places in 1997, and the Mansell House and Gardens, a 1912 Queen Anne home, hosts events and houses the Alpharetta Historical Society.

On the entertainment side, Ameris Bank Amphitheatre holds 12,000 people and is the summer home of the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra. A weekly farmers market runs downtown from April to October, and the Brew Moon Fest takes over downtown on the first Saturday of October.

Fulton County Schools serves the city, and Alpharetta High School serves most of it. Families sometimes also look at Cambridge, Centennial, Chattahoochee, Johns Creek, Milton, Northview and Roswell high schools, depending on the address.

Elementary schools listed for the city include Abbotts Hill, Alpharetta Elementary, Creek View, Dolvin, Lake Windward, Manning Oaks and New Prospect, and Amana Academy is a public charter for kindergarten through eighth grade. Perimeter College at Georgia State University, Gwinnett Technical College and Reinhardt University each have a campus here. Confirm the attendance zone with the school district before putting a school name in your listing.

sections.h2: Is the address inside Alpharetta city limits?
sections.html:
An Alpharetta mailing address does not guarantee the property lies inside the city. The Halcyon mixed-use district has an Alpharetta postal address yet sits in Forsyth County, outside both the city limits and Fulton County.

That changes who bills the property. The City of Alpharetta levies its own ad valorem tax for city operations and voter-approved bonds and keeps its own homestead exemption page, while Fulton County sets the assessment. A parcel in a neighboring jurisdiction owes tax to different governments. Read your tax bill, or ask the county assessors which governments tax the parcel, before you tell a buyer what the house costs to carry.

sections.h2: How do Fulton County assessment appeals work for Alpharetta owners?
sections.html:
Fulton sends each property a yearly notice of assessment, and owners who dispute the fair market value it states get 45 days from the notice date to respond. The county says the value is the only thing open to appeal, and the right ends after the deadline printed on the notice.

  • Filing is online, by mail, or in person at five county sites, one of them the North Fulton center at 7741 Roswell Road NE, Suite 210.
  • The form asks you to pick a hearing path, and arbitration or a hearing officer can add fees.
  • Review can take months, and a temporary bill that arrives meanwhile still has to be paid.

Mention an unresolved appeal to your closing attorney before the settlement date.

sections.h2: Which city services and permits matter when selling in Alpharetta?
sections.html:
The city's Apply menu gathers the forms a seller may need: a permitting portal, building construction permits, business licenses, homestead exemptions, and a form to establish or end trash service. Water and sewer bills are paid to Fulton County, so closing that account is a separate step from ending city trash service.

The city also keeps a Short-Term Rentals page under its Business section. If you plan to tell a buyer the house can host nightly guests, get the current rules from the city's planning and zoning staff in writing first. Before closing, look up any deck, finished basement or HVAC replacement in the permitting portal so an unfinished permit does not hold things up.

sections.h2: How does the deed transfer tax apply to an Alpharetta sale?
sections.html:
The transfer tax is an excise on the sale itself, separate from the yearly property tax, and the clerk will not record the deed until it is settled. Alpharetta deeds are recorded in Fulton County, and the state clerks' authority supplies the PT-61 form that reports the sale.

The seller owes it by default. For questions on whether a gift, family or trust transfer is taxable, the revenue department points owners to the county clerk, so call that office before closing.

faqs.q: How far apart are Alpharetta's home values and Albany's?
faqs.a: Very far. The Census Bureau lists $649,000 for Alpharetta's typical owner-occupied home against $124,300 in Albany and $299,200 in Athens-Clarke County for 2020-2024.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff for a Fulton appeal on Alpharetta property?
faqs.a: Fulton allows 45 days from the date on the Notice of Assessment. The date printed on your notice controls, and the appeal covers value only.

faqs.q: Does a 30004 or 30005 mailing address prove the house is in the city?
faqs.a: No. Halcyon, for instance, uses an Alpharetta address but sits in Forsyth County. Check your tax bill or ask the Fulton County Board of Assessors.

faqs.q: Who carries the transfer tax in an Alpharetta contract?
faqs.a: The seller by default, though a contract clause can hand the cost to the buyer. Ask your closing attorney to confirm the amount before the settlement date.

faqs.q: What should I do about an unfinished permit before selling?
faqs.a: Ask the city's building permit staff through the permitting portal what is open on the address, and tell the buyer about any permit that has not been finished and approved.
